AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #2
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Overgrazing continuously

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Inorganic fertilisers? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Inorganic fertilisers.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Inorganic fertilisers.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Inorganic fertilisers.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Inorganic fertilisers.

4. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Paper burning to ash

5. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. watt (W)
   D. joule (J)

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Health: Parasite control? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Health: Parasite control.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Health: Parasite control.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Health: Parasite control.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Health: Parasite control.

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Rearing Selected Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Rearing Selected Animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Rearing Selected Animals.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Rearing Selected Animals.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Rearing Selected Animals.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Protection: Pest control? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Pest control.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Protection: Pest control.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Protection: Pest control.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Protection: Pest control.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agroforestry? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agroforestry.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agroforestry.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Agroforestry.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agroforestry.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Livestock Products? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Livestock Products.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Livestock Products.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Livestock Products.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Livestock Products.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structures in Animal production? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structures in Animal production.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structures in Animal production.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Structures in Animal production.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structures in Animal production.

13. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Digestive systems of animals? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Digestive systems of animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Digestive systems of animals.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Digestive systems of animals.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Digestive systems of animals.

15. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Production Structures? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Production Structures.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Production Structures.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Production Structures.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Production Structures.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Crop Protection: Pest control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Crop Production Structures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Digestive systems of animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Health: Parasite control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Structures in Animal production and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Aquaculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
